title: Signal Weft: Quant Research Weekly Capture
content:
Context:
This note is a compact capture from the applied-ml research sync (02/08/2026) focused on three parallel tracks: compact quant probes, eval drift detection, and onboarding one new family (rw-13b-slim). Goal: capture what we observed this week, what we will prioritize, and quick action items so engineers can pick up next steps without digging through threads.

Attendees:
- Anika Shah (owner)
- Marcus Lin (quant infra)
- Priya Patel (evals & metrics)
- Diego Ramos (serving-runtime)
- Yiming Chen (SRE, joined for KV cache discussion)

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- INT4 symmetric per-channel (calibrated on calibration set) gives ~2.4x memory reduction vs FP16 on rw-13b-slim with measured 6–8% degradation on open-domain QA accuracy; latency improved at 50-token sequences but regressed for short (<16) sequences due to extra dequant/requant hotspots.
- Observed a KV-cache regression on a microbatching path when switching to fused int kernels; root cause likely related to K/V alignment padding in the runtime.
- Evals detected a small but consistent drop (0.9–1.6%) on our safety regression suite when applying layerwise outlier clamping during quantization — more investigation required to determine if clamp or calibration set is cause.

Experiments and results (concise)
1) rw-13b-slim — INT4 symmetric per-channel (experiment id QW-2026-021)
   - Setup: calibration set = 4k tokens sampled from customer-sim corpus; static post-training quant (no finetune); runtime: fused int kernels on A100 Ampere.
   - Memory: FP16 peak model size 13.2GB => INT4 model 5.3GB (measured payload reduction ~60%).
   - Throughput: steady-state throughput increased 1.9x for 512-token contexts when batching 8.
   - Latency: median token latency for 50-token responses improved ~12%; median latency for 8-token responses increased ~18% due to dequant path in emission loop.
   - Quality: QA F1 (dev-sampled) dropped from 75.4 to 69.8 (7.4% absolute drop). Perplexity on held-out LM subset increased from 18.2 -> 20.6 (~13% relative).
   - Early interpretation: Good cost wins for long-form, not a drop-in replacement for low-latency short-turn interactions.

2) KV-cache regression (issue observed after switching to fused int GEMM kernels)
   - Symptom: occasional hallucinated repeats and token stutter when serving interactive streams with cached KV across requests.
   - Repro: deterministic in stress harness when sending repeated generation calls with cached prefix length 384 and microbatch size 4.
   - Hypothesis: buffer alignment off-by-eight when quantized weights use group packing; runtime copy path incorrectly computes kv_offset in bytes vs elements in some fused code path.
   - Short-term mitigation: fall back to non-fused int kernels for cached routes (cfg flag enabled in runtime).
   - Owner: Diego to land fallback gate; Marcus to add unit tests for kv_offset alignment.

3) Safety regression delta after layerwise outlier clamping (experiment id QW-2026-024)
   - Change: during calibration we applied per-channel clamp at 3.5 sigma to limit extreme weight values.
   - Observation: small regression on safety suites (toxicity + policy triggers increased by ~1%).
   - Next check: re-run with different clamp thresholds (2.5, 3.0, 4.0) and with a calibration set that matches safety prompt distribution (Priya to provision).

Open questions (prioritized)
- Is the short-sequence latency regression from quant math (dequant cost) or from branching/conditional code introduced by kernel fusion? (Diego + Marcus)
- What thresholds for per-channel clamps preserve safety without losing headroom for compression? (Priya + Anika)
- For rw-13b-slim, is there a narrow finetune recipe (100M tokens) that recovers ~3–4% QA F1 while keeping INT4 benefits? (Research spike)

Action items (owners and ETA)
- Diego: land runtime gate to disable fused int kernels when prefix_cache is enabled. ETA: 02/10/2026. Linked PR: runtime#987.
- Marcus: add unit/regression tests for kv_offset alignment and push microbenchmark harness for short-context token latency across kernel variants. ETA: 02/12/2026.
- Priya: prepare targeted calibration set for safety prompts and run clamp threshold sweep (2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0) with logging for per-example deltas. ETA: 02/15/2026.
- Anika: design a small fine-tune recipe proposal (data sources, compute estimate, expected gains) for rw-13b-slim INT4 viability; sync with research. ETA: 02/18/2026.
- All: add short notes to the quant-runbook (confluence) about observed tradeoffs for long vs short contexts; include decision matrix for using INT4 vs FP16 per route. ETA: 02/14/2026.

Notes for product/solutions teams (what to say to customers)
- Short messaging: "We’re seeing strong memory and cost wins from 4-bit quantization on long-context workloads, with some measurable quality tradeoffs on short-turn low-latency interactions — we will gate fused kernels for interactive routes and continue tuning calibration/finetune options."
- For Dedicated customers using real-time chat routes, we should recommend sticking to FP16 or staged rollout with the runtime fallback until KV-cache fusion issues are resolved.

Parking lot / future experiments
- Explore mixed-mode: FP16 for attention layers + INT4 for FFN (quick ablation plan).
- Investigate per-head quant thresholds (selectively higher precision on top-k heads).
- Run a small RLHF-style recovery finetune (low compute) for models degraded by quant clamps.

Misc notes and quick links
- Microbenchmark logs uploaded: s3://redwood-internal/quant/microbench/2026-02-08/ (Marcus)
- Stress harness reproducer: github.com/redwood-inference/quant-repro under tests/stress/kv-alignment

Meeting wrap-up (02/08/2026)
- Decision: enable runtime fallback for cached routes immediately (safety-first).
- Agreement: run clamp sweep in parallel with kernel fallback work.
- Next sync: quick check-in 02/12/2026 (15 min) to confirm PRs and sweeps, full research sync 02/18/2026 to review finetune proposal.

Notes to self (Anika)
- Keep an eye on customer usage patterns — if a subset of customers are heavy long-context generators, they are good candidates for INT4 opt-in Beta.
- Document a short FAQ for sales/solutions: expected mem delta, latency caveats, recommended routes.
